mentl/c801559:
Checker-in-WASM printed len(env)=14 where the bare path prints 15.
Traced the off-by-one to a latent bug in std/compiler/lower.lux:
extract_handler_entry at line 858 only recognizes ResumeExpr or
BlockExpr-ending-in-ResumeExpr as handler body shapes — any other
shape falls through to `updates=[]`, silently discarding the state
update. Line 262's `ResumeExpr(value, _) => lower_expr(value, env)`
then drops the `updates` field of any nested resume with `_`,
completing the elision.

The bind handler's body was an IfExpr of the shape
`if is_existing_builtin { resume(()) } else { resume(()) with state = (...) }`.
extract_handler_entry fell through, emitted the entire if as the
resume value with empty updates, and the inner `resume(()) with
state = ...` in the else branch lowered as just `i32.const 0`.
bind was a no-op at the WASM handler dispatch level — every
let-binding recorded during WASM execution of check_program was
silently dropped.

This commit rewrites bind into the canonical form that push_scope,
pop_scope, fresh_eff, and track_effect already use: compute the new
state value conditionally via a `let`, then issue `resume(()) with
state = (...)` unconditionally at the tail. Semantically identical
to the original. A load-bearing comment on the handler warns future
authors not to "clean up" the indirection without reading the
reproduction crucibles first.

The proper fix — teaching lower.lux to recognize IfExpr (and
MatchExpr) handler bodies and lift state updates into conditional
LIf values that `subst_state_to_cells` already walks correctly —
is deliberately deferred. This workaround unblocks wasm_check.lux
validation without risk to the handler-emission path across the
rest of the language.

Reproduction crucibles added alongside:

- examples/conditional_resume.lux       minimal bug repro — bare: 10, WASM: 0
- examples/conditional_resume_fixed.lux canonical-form fix — bare: 10, WASM: 10
- examples/mini_primitives.lux          14-step list-cons |> chain; rules ou

bits/c87017a:
Grabs are per finger now. There used to be one, so a second hand stole
the first one's puppet and ended its pass where it was touched — two
people could not play at once, which is what a puppet show is. Each
finger keeps its own grab, each releases its own pass, and one finger
per channel is the rule so two hands on the same puppet cannot record
two passes fighting over it.

Perform mode is the stage and nothing else: no title strip, no timeline,
no dock, no halo. Just the record button and a way out. The stage keeps
its 9:16 and grows to the full height of the window — performing in one
shape and rendering in another would make a puppet a different shape in
the film than on the stage it was performed on.

A blind take now ends in a reveal. You perform against an empty stage,
and when you stop, a curtain parts on the whole show playing itself
back. Meeting it is the point of recording blind; being told to go and
press play is not.

Nine new assertions, including two fingers driving two puppets into two
separate passes, driven through raw CDP touch points because
page.touchscreen carries only one. 59/59 checks pass.
